title: Phone layout in desktop-site mode
description: A phone that asks for the desktop site (Chrome / Safari 'Request desktop site') lays the page out about 980 px wide, so the (max-width: 720px) media queries never matched: no slim top bar, no minimize pills, 32 px buttons. The layout is now decided once in script (useCompactLayout.ts): compact when the viewport is phone sized (as before), OR the device is touch only (pointer coarse + hover none, or touch points with no fine pointer) with a physical screen whose short side is 600 px or less, OR the manual override says so. The decision is mirrored on <html data-layout> (and data-layout-forced when the viewport is wide) and a build-time PostCSS step repeats every phone @media block under :where(:root[data-layout-forced]), so every phone rule applies in desktop-site mode too. iPads (short side 744 px and up) and mouse desktops keep the desktop layout. Menu > Layout (Auto / Phone / Desktop) and ?layout=compact|desktop|auto override the decision. The before shots force the desktop layout, which is what the phone got before. Decision dialogs were already minimizable everywhere (the control is script driven, not media-query driven); what was missing in desktop-site mode was the 44 px size and the phone chrome. Synthetic fixtures through a mocked server, emulated devices (980x2121 layout viewport, 390x844 screen, coarse pointer, no hover).

shots.caption: The whole map is visible and tappable; the pill ('Resume decision') brings the dialog back and it stays minimized until a new decision arrives.

shots.caption: Auto / Phone / Desktop; the choice is stored in localStorage (ti4.layout.v1) and wins over the detection.

shots.heading: ?layout=compact on a 1440x900 desktop
shots.caption: The URL parameter stores the override and is removed from the address; ?layout=auto clears it.
